page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU features a dedicated allocation model, 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local storage and bundled GPU resources, and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core testing placing in the top 25% at 2681.08. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weak, scoring 5386.56 in stress-ng multi-core and 3257.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only operations on large blocks registering at 38.56 GB/sec, though write operations on large blocks achieve an average tier of 28.03 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without demanding high multi-core compute performance. Given the weak multi-core and database benchmark results, this instance is best suited for memory-bound single-threaded applications, lightweight caching layers, text processing, and small-scale LLM text generation.
